name: Cnoc Sídhe Úna

attributes.attribute: the Tipperary hill of the fairy queen Úna
known in English as Knockshegouna or Knockshigowna

text: Cnoc Sídhe Úna is a prominent hill in north County Tipperary, Ireland. It rises 699 feet and stands about two miles east of Ballingarry. Tradition makes the hill a home of the fairies and holds it sacred to Úna, their queen. Her name stays attached to the summit in the English forms Knockshegouna and Knockshigowna. The hill also carried older ritual life. People once held Lughnasa activities on its slopes.

okr.objective: Cnoc Sídhe Úna is the Tipperary hill held sacred to the fairy queen Úna.
key_results: A prominent hill of 699 feet stands in north County Tipperary, two miles east of Ballingarry.
